answer: Every new key must anchor itself to a measured network position: independent landmarks time randomized probes, and the key must mirror those latency vectors consistently across rounds. Keys resolving to the same ASN, host, or timing fingerprint are merged into one voice, much as repeated umber brushstrokes read as a single smear. A farmer can mint unlimited keys but must rent and keep alive genuinely separate machines in many regions; spoofed coordinates fail cross-probes. Cost is ongoing distributed hosting, not a one-off registration fee.
